Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

reprokit 0.1.0

First release (lifecycle: experimental). Not on CRAN; names and output may change.

Share: for authors who cannot share raw data

  • sufficient_stats(x, ..., threshold = 5) says whether summary statistics make an analysis reproducible without the raw data, what to publish and what readers lose, and stores the summaries at full precision. It never errors on the verdict (apa_suffices, apa_plus_suffices or needs_raw_data); the printed object narrates the verdict, what to publish, what readers lose and which group or cell a disclosure flag fired for. Only invalid input is an error of class reprokit_impossible.
  • The verdict is a tier around the APA set. apa_suffices: the numbers APA style asks for determine the result. apa_plus_suffices: a few more numbers are needed, and the advice names each one, says why, and, where the APA numbers bound it, gives the range they imply (“r is implied between .60 and .64 by the APA numbers; reporting it makes the result exact”). Each handler declares these additions, and coverage_table() shows the tier per test. Simple regression is apa_suffices because r follows exactly from the standardized beta, sign(b) times the square root of R-squared, or t over the square root of t-squared plus df. A goodness-of-fit test needs the null proportions only when they are not equal. Every verdict ends by saying that sharing the raw data remains the standard. Synthetic data is not a verdict; the advice mentions it only, as outside reprokit, for analyses with no finite summaries.
  • sufficient_stats(test = "paired", n = "30", m = c("5.1", "4.6"), sd = c("1.2", "1.3")) takes typed numbers as strings, with the same names, parsing and checks as check_reported(), and returns a verdict and the additions (present, missing or implied with a range). It holds no summaries, so appendix() refuses it.
  • check_reported() ends with one line, “Also report … to make this fully checkable.”
  • Appendix labels use the symbols APA style uses: eta squared, omega squared, partial eta squared, partial omega squared, R squared, adjusted R squared, beta (standardized) and d.
  • What readers lose is stated by reprokit, from the test (sufficient_stats(...)$lost); it is not an argument.
  • appendix(x, ..., sharing_reason, choices = list()) writes a Markdown appendix: the numbers APA style asks for, the numbers it does not but the result needs, the analysis choices, the numbers a reader cannot check, why the data are not shared, what readers lose, and a disclosure check. Underneath, it reproduces the result from the stored statistics and refuses if it does not match the original analysis. sharing_reason is optional and reprokit never suggests one: without it appendix() warns and the appendix says “Reason for not sharing the raw data: not stated by the author.”
  • Model input. sufficient_stats() and appendix() accept an lm, aov or chisq.test() result, and a t.test() or cor.test() result together with data. Choices recorded in a result (tails, confidence level, Student or Welch, test value, continuity correction, H0 proportions) are read from it and marked “read from the result”. A result that does not match its data is refused, and so is a data.name that cannot be mapped to the data (with a hint to the formula route). A formula with data and test still works for any covered test.
  • appendix(x, ..., extra = character()) adds a section of further numbers, computed from the stored summaries and formatted as APA asks: pass names, or "all". The R squared family where the test has one (eta squared, omega squared, R squared, adjusted R squared, partial effect sizes, per-model R squared and F of a mediation) and standardized betas for a regression. Invalid names are an input error that lists the valid extras; the default appendix is unchanged. coverage_table() has an extras column.
  • Given a model or a test result, appendix() prints the numbers the model itself holds (summary() of the lm, the aov table, the htest fields). Each is also recomputed from the stored summaries; a fit that differs by more than the round-trip tolerance is refused with reprokit_impossible.
  • Mediation: sufficient_stats(lm(M ~ X), lm(Y ~ X + M)) stores n, the means and the covariance of X, M and Y.
  • Handlers (handlers()): t_independent, t_one_sample, t_paired, cor_pearson, anova_oneway, anova_factorial, chisq_independence, chisq_gof, lm_simple, lm_multiple, lm_moderation, mediation_simple, and a general lm handler that shares and reproduces but has no coverage row and no check route.
    • anova_factorial (two-factor between-subjects) stores n, mean and SD per cell. The pooled error term (equal variances) is listed as lost. The sums of squares type is a declared choice in unbalanced designs.
    • The chi-squared handlers store the counts; low expected counts are listed as lost, not checked.
    • mediation_simple lists the bootstrap CI of the indirect effect as lost, and gives the missing correlations of X, M and Y their own reason (the paths b and c’ depend on how X and M overlap).
  • Disclosure check per test. The default threshold is 5 and applies to groups, cells, counts and factor levels; the general minimum n stays 2 x threshold.
    • chisq_independence flags a cell and chisq_gof a category with 0 < count < threshold. A count of 0 is not flagged: a zero can reveal an attribute of a whole group, but flagging it would also flag every sparse table.
    • lm_multiple, lm_moderation and the general lm flag every factor level with fewer than threshold rows in the fit, counted unweighted (rows with weight 0 are not in the fit). The check of 0/1 columns and their pairwise tables stays.
    • t_one_sample, t_paired, cor_pearson and mediation_simple, which have no groups or cells, say so, so the appendix always names what was checked (“sample size only (no groups or cells; no individual values stored)”).
    • A flag drops the verdict to needs_raw_data. The check lowers the risk of identifying a participant; it is not a guarantee of anonymity.

Check: for readers of a paper

  • check_reported(test, ...) tests whether reported numbers are consistent with each other. test is one of "student", "welch", "one_sample", "paired", "pearson", "oneway", "factorial", "chisq", "gof", "mediation", "lm", "lm_simple" or "lm_moderation", given first or as test =. Numbers are given as strings, so their decimals define rounding intervals. The output gives a verdict, a coverage level (0 to 3), a status for each number, the analysis variants that fit, and the ranges implied for numbers that were not reported. An inconsistency never says which number is wrong.
  • Each test accepts the quantities that apply to it. A known name that does not apply (d for a correlation) is an input error listing the names the test takes. The R squared family is cross-checked where it exists: Pearson r2 and adj_r2, one-way r2 (identical to eta2), eta2, r2 and omega2 from t and df, partial effect sizes in a factorial ANOVA, adj_r2 in a regression, and per-model r2 and F in a mediation. Student degrees of freedom are checked against the group sizes when the test is declared "student", and the hint for a missing number no longer lists a relation another one already covers.
  • Pearson: r is not reported as “not checkable” when it reaches p only through an unreported t (for example check_reported("pearson", r = ".41", df = "28", p = ".024")).
  • Chi-squared: the table of counts (a matrix, or a vector for goodness of fit) and the reported chi-squared, df, p, N and Cramer’s V (Cohen’s w for goodness of fit). The table shape (dims) and the H0 proportions (p0) are test arguments: df is checked only when the shape is known. Yates’ correction is a variant for a 2 x 2 table, shared by chi-squared and p; V and w are conventions that never make a report inconsistent, and a reported phi is compared by absolute value. An expected count of 0 is not evaluable.
  • Test arguments: mu, dims, p0, k, mediator, and effect ("A", "B" or "AB") for factorial designs; a handler rejects one it does not declare.
  • Factorial ANOVA: checked from the cell matrices. The sums of squares type (III, II,
    1. is a variant shared by F, p and partial eta squared; a balanced design has none. Partial eta squared and partial omega squared are conventions. Exact F ranges are used for one-df effects and balanced main effects; other effects are checked for coherence only.
  • One-way ANOVA: a negative omega squared (F < 1) reported in the eta2 slot is accepted; the eta2 domain is [-1, 1], as for the factorial ANOVA.
  • Regression ("lm", "lm_simple", "lm_moderation"): t = b / SE, p from t and the residual df, the CI at 90, 95 or 99 per cent, F from R squared with df1 and df2, p from F, and the n implied by df2 = n - k - 1. Per-term numbers are vectors named by term. k is a test argument or is read from df1; it is never guessed from the number of terms given, so without it n is not checkable. A simple regression adds R squared = r squared, t squared = F and r = b SD_x / SD_y. Adjusted R squared and beta are conventions that never make a report inconsistent.
  • Mediation: the paths a, b, c and c’ are checked as regression coefficients (t from b and SE, p from t and df, with df = n - 2 or n - 3). A reported CI of a path (ci_lower, ci_upper, named by path) is checked from b, SE, the path’s df and the level (90, 95 or 99 per cent); it is optional. The reported indirect effect is checked against the product of the rounding intervals of a and b; if it falls outside, the result says “not coherent” (a bootstrap mean can differ a little from the product). The indirect effect’s CI is not checkable, and no Sobel-type test is computed.
  • appendix() for the regression rows asks for the confidence level of the intervals and, for the three lm rows, the R squared convention (R squared or adjusted R squared): choices = list(level = "0.95", convention = "r2"). Mediation asks for the level only. Both appear in block C, “not declared” when not given.

Coverage

  • Independent-samples t-test (Student and Welch), paired-samples t-test, one-sample t-test, Pearson correlation, one-way and two-factor between-subjects ANOVA, chi-squared tests of independence and goodness of fit, simple, multiple and moderation regression, and simple mediation.
  • coverage_table() lists, per test, what APA style asks to report, what the result needs, what is missing and why, what can be checked, and which choices must be declared. It is generated from the registry. The coverage row for simple mediation reads: checkable “a, b, c, c’ (b, SE, t, p, CI each)”, sufficient “n, M, SD and correlations of X, M, Y”, missing “the correlations of X, M, Y”.
  • conventions() lists the effect-size conventions (choices$convention) and sums-of-squares types (choices$ss_type) each handler accepts, with the default and the appendix label. It reads the registry that appendix() validates against.
  • appendix() uses type III when a factorial ANOVA’s SS type is not declared and says so: “type III (reprokit default, not stated by the author)”, because a fitted aov does not record it. Checking a paper still tries III, II and I. An undeclared effect-size convention of a one-way ANOVA is shown as not declared.

Documentation

  • New vignettes: vignette("reprokit") (getting started), vignette("concepts") (terms) and vignette("validation") (evidence). The validation vignette reads the committed results of the scripts in inst/validation/results/, each stamped with its seed, the package version and the date.
  • The README is generated from README.Rmd, with the coverage table rendered from coverage_table().
  • The package help page (?reprokit) gives an overview of both directions.

check_reported() additions

  • A “coherent” number now says which relation would verify it and what that needs (for example “t_from_descriptives would verify it (needs n, m, sd)”).
  • With the test declared as Student, df is checked against n alone (df = n1 + n2 - 2); Welch is never held to it. d is cross-checked from t and n (not falsifying).
  • eta squared (omega squared) of the t tests is checked from t and df; R squared of Pearson’s r from r; simple mediation checks R squared, F and p per model.
